text:
alex: heads-up — I hit a weird SDK parity bug with streaming. Node client drops chunk ordering after a client disconnect that happens during an auth refresh. python client (same sample app) resumes fine.

maya: ugh. sample app or prod?

alex: sample-app locally. Node SDK v0.12.3, Python SDK v0.9.7. repro steps below.

alex: repro (short):
1) start streaming request from sample-app (SSE).
2) force token refresh in the middle (short TTL + revoke) so auth refresh kicks in.
3) immediately kill the client network (simulate mobile switching networks) -> client reconnects.
4) Node reconnect comes back with fragments interleaved / out-of-order; python reconnect uses Last-Event-ID and replays missing fragments correctly.

alex: logs from node run: 
```
[stream] received fragment:{"id":1001,"chunk":"hello\n"}
[auth] refreshing token
[network] disconnect
[reconnect] new connection established
[stream] received fragment:{"id":1003,"chunk":"world\n"}
[stream] received fragment:{"id":1002,"chunk":" there\n"}
```
node output shows 1003 then 1002. python logs: 1001, 1002, 1003.

sam: can you paste the client connect code? is Node using the eventsource polyfill?

alex: yep. sample-app uses `eventsource` in node env. connection options: include `Authorization` header, and we set `lastEventId` from resume token. code snippet: 
```
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${tok}` } });
es.addEventListener('message', onMsg);
// on reconnect we set es.reconnectLastEventId = lastId;
```
(we tried manually setting `Last-Event-ID` header but the polyfill ignores it on auth refresh path)

maya: so the polyfill doesn't persist last-event-id across the auth-refresh dance? sounds like race where new auth request occurs and we open a fresh EventSource without attaching the last id header before server sends second chunk.

leo: quick guess — when token refresh triggers, node flow does `close()` then `new EventSource()` after auth, but we attach `message` listener async after the connection's first frames. If the server pushes queued tokens immediately, the first fragments can arrive before handler/last-id is attached. python probably attaches synchronously or passes ID in constructor.

sam: got it. can you try constructing EventSource with `headers` that include `Last-Event-ID` from the resume token and ensure it's part of the initial request?

alex: tried that; the polyfill's constructor accepts headers but when using our SDK's auth-refresh wrapper, the fresh EventSource is created before resume token is computed in the auth callback. race.

alex: minimal repro I'm going to push: sample-app branch `devex/sse-repro-node` — it toggles TTL to 5s and forces a disconnect at +6s to exercise race.

maya: small mitigation: if SDK ensures resume token is resolved and stuck into `url` as query param (e.g., `?resume_id=...`) then server can use that without waiting for headers. not ideal but works as fallback.

leo: agree. better fix: ensure EventSource constructed with the resume id synchronously after auth completes, and attach listeners before opening. Or wrap connection open in a promise that waits until resume token available.

sam: will file a proper issue in sdk-node repo w/ label devex/streaming and assign to @sam. alex — can you attach the node logs and the tiny repro branch?

alex: done. branch pushed and logs attached in the issue. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/42 (repro + small test).

devex-bot: CI for pr #42 passed :white_check_mark: (tests: unit/streaming-parity).

maya: thanks. next steps: (1) add synchronous resume-id injection as a short-term patch, (2) add an e2e in CI that simulates auth refresh + disconnect, (3) update docs in SDK quickstart for mobile network churn notes.

alex: I'll open a PR with the patch for node and a follow-up PR to add CI e2e. marking as blocker for SDK parity milestone. :thumbsup:

sam: nice work. tagging eng-runtime to watch server behavior in case we need tolerant ordering.

leo: FYI — I saw a flaky failing test in our internal streaming harness that matches this pattern. will cross-link.

alex: cool. if anyone wants to repro locally: git clone, checkout branch, `npm i && npm run start-repro` then flip airplane mode after 6s.

maya: appreciated — short and actionable.

sam: thanks alex! :rocket:
